notes: Candidate matches the session: an inclusive keyset cursor (`id >= $2`) was made strict in the query, a regression test was added, and the full suite passed. It names the specific problem class (keyset pagination, inclusive vs strict cursor comparison). The one decision states the real alternative (handler row-drop) and the reason the session gives (deleted cursor row would be skipped). Skills were all used; 'keyset pagination' is closer to a topic than a skill but is not padding.
verdicts.summary: Fixed a keyset pagination defect where an inclusive cursor comparison repeated the last invoice of one page at the top of the next, by making the query comparison strict. Added a regression test, and the full Go test suite passed.
decisions: Made the cursor comparison strict in the query rather than dropping the first row in the handler, because the handler workaround would silently skip a real row if the cursor record had been deleted.
